extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers and practitioners working on story generation and creative-language models
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating neural models that generate multi-sentence stories conditioned on prompts, using a hierarchical approach (generate a premise then expand to a passage) and mechanisms for long-range context. Evaluation uses both automated metrics and human judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence and fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative systems that can build coherent and fluent passages of text about a topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper frames story generation quality in terms of producing passages that are both coherent (logical, consistent narrative over multiple sentences) and fluent (natural-sounding language). Improvements are reported against strong baselines on these aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchical generation (premise → passage)
rubrics_metrics.description: The model first generates a premise, and then transforms it into a passage of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors propose and evaluate a hierarchical approach where an intermediate premise is generated before the full story; this pipeline is presented as a means to improve overall story quality compared to non-hierarchical models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to the prompt
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevance of the generated story to the given writing prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper introduces a novel form of model fusion intended to improve how well the story matches the prompt; relevance is an explicit objective and axis of evaluation (measured via automated and human evaluations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling long-range context
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to capture long-range dependencies across a story (multi-sentence / paragraph-level context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They add a gated multi-scale self-attention mechanism to model long-range context, arguing that handling long-range context is crucial for coherent multi-sentence story generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training data: large paired prompt–story corpus
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a large dataset of human-written stories paired with writing prompts (the authors collected ~300K pairs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper emphasizes that a large paired dataset enables hierarchical generation and improved performance — implying dataset scale and prompt–story alignment are important practical requirements for training effective story-generation models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation methods: automated metrics and human judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess model outputs with both automated evaluation metrics and human evaluations (preferences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments report large improvements on both automated and human evaluations; specifically, human judges preferred the authors' hierarchical approach to a strong non-hierarchical model by roughly two-to-one, indicating human preference studies are a critical evaluation component.
